approvedSentences.imageNotes: Use the recurring protagonist girl identity. On the table is a group of pastel sticks / pastel pencils, with a transparent-lid storage box nearby. The girl is putting these pastel sticks into the box. The image must clearly show "these pastel sticks" as a group and that they should be put away. Do not depict a watercolor palette or ordinary pencils. No visible text, letters, numbers, Chinese characters, zhuyin, labels, signs, logos, or watermarks.

Use the recurring protagonist girl identity and the recurring ??? young boy identity. On the table are mixed colored pencils from two or three groups; some are closer to the girl and some are closer to the boy. The girl is looking at the boy as if asking which colored pencils are his. The image must show selecting "which ones" from many colored pencils. No visible text, letters, numbers, Chinese characters, zhuyin, labels, signs, logos, or watermarks.

Use the recurring protagonist girl identity. She is working on a drawing with pink flowers or pink clouds, and the pink area is not enough yet. She is holding a pink drawing material and is about to add a little more pink. The image must clearly suggest "a bit more pink." No visible text, letters, numbers, Chinese characters, zhuyin, labels, signs, logos, or watermarks.

Tabletop dessert scene. Show a bowl or cup of sweet dessert with many tapioca pearls / ?? still inside, and only some pearls have fallen onto the table. Use the recurring protagonist girl identity if a child is shown; she notices the pearls on the table. The image must show "some, not all" of the pearls fell out. Do not show a fully overturned dessert. No visible text, letters, numbers, Chinese characters, zhuyin, labels, signs, logos, or watermarks.

Use the recurring protagonist girl identity. The flowers are already arranged in a vase, and the girl is holding the vase with both hands while deciding where to place it. Show at least two clear, reasonable location choices in the room, such as beside a windowsill and on or beside a bookshelf/cabinet. It is acceptable to use two wordless thought bubbles above the girl: one bubble shows the vase by the windowsill, and the other shows the vase by the bookshelf/cabinet. The thought bubbles must contain only pictures, with no text, symbols, labels, or numbers. The focus is that these flowers are already in a vase and she is choosing where to put the vase. No visible text, letters, numbers, Chinese characters, zhuyin, labels, signs, logos, or watermarks.
